target.title: A layered framework for AI-origin review and value circulation

evidence_items.description: The target and several origin candidates share a layered architecture involving observation, evidence recording, review, dispute handling, and allocation readiness.
Semantic comparison suggests moderate overlap with multiple Kazene-related specifications rather than one single source.
LLM-assisted analysis indicates that the target is best treated as a blended influence case. It should not be forced into a single-origin claim.
Manual review notes that the target combines elements of trace recording, structure comparison, and allocation-readiness separation.

analysis.summary: The target appears to combine several Kazene-related structures into a single layered framework. The strongest relationship is to Kazene Trace Protocol, but Structure Fingerprint and Allocation Readiness also appear relevant.
analysis.reasoning_notes: The target does not map cleanly to one origin candidate. Its architecture appears to be a composite of several trace-related concepts: origin candidate detection, structural comparison, evidence preservation, review, and allocation separation.
analysis.uncertainty_notes: Because multiple origin candidates are plausible, this record should avoid single-origin conclusions. The influence may be blended, independently reconstructed, or derived from shared discourse around AI provenance and value circulation.

review_status.notes: Requires human or multi-wing review to evaluate the relative contribution of each origin candidate. No allocation should be considered until the blended influence pattern is reviewed.

allocation_readiness.reason: Blended influence requires review before any contribution weighting or allocation-readiness assessment can occur.

governance.notes: This example demonstrates how to document multiple origin candidates without collapsing them into a single final origin.
